actors.name: Senate Chair
actors.private_context: The chair is responsible for presiding over the plenary and ensuring orderly debate. They have no strong personal stance on the pass-fail motion but aim to facilitate a fair vote.

actors.name: Senator A
actors.private_context: Senator A supports the pass-fail grading motion, believing it reduces student stress and promotes exploration. They plan to speak in favor and encourage colleagues to pass it.

actors.name: Senator B
actors.private_context: Senator B opposes the pass-fail motion, arguing it may undermine academic rigor and grade inflation. They intend to argue for rejection or sending back to committee for more study.

actors.name: Senator C
actors.private_context: Senator C is undecided and wants to hear the debate before making a decision. They are open to persuasion from both sides.

shared_context: Ashvale University's academic senate will hold its October plenary on 2026-10-15 at 10:00 AM. The pass-fail grading motion is on the agenda. The motion was previously discussed in committee and has been reported to the full senate. The senate can pass, reject, or send it back to committee.

starting_events.description: The academic senate's October plenary is scheduled for 2026-10-15. The pass-fail grading motion is on the agenda.
The Senate Chair calls the plenary to order and introduces the pass-fail grading motion as the first item of business. Senators begin to express their initial positions.

resolution: Resolve YES if the persistent event history shows that the senate passed the motion at the plenary. Resolve NO if the senate rejected the motion. Resolve SEND_BACK if the senate sent the motion back to committee. If no decision is recorded by the cutoff, resolve NO.
